lesson.title: Which folds match?
lesson.subtitle: P4 symmetry revision
lesson.objective: Find the lines of symmetry of a shape.
lesson.story: Test four dashed lines on a rhombus.

steps.title: Test the dashed lines
steps.prompt: Which of the dashed lines are lines of symmetry? Choose every line that works.
hints: A line of symmetry splits the shape into two halves that match exactly when folded.
Imagine folding the shape along each line. Do the two sides land exactly on each other?
Test one line at a time. A line that only looks balanced may not work.
Choose line B and line C.

steps.title: Count all the lines
steps.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have in all?
hints: Look for every different way to fold the shape so the halves match.
The dashed lines show only some of the ways. Think about other folds.
Count each different fold that works. There are more than one.
A rhombus has 2 lines of symmetry. Enter 2.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How can you tell if a line is a line of symmetry?

choices.label: Fold along it: the two halves must match exactly.
The line goes through the very middle of the whole shape.
The line joins two of the opposite corners of the shape.

hints: A line through the middle does not always work.
A line joining corners does not always work either.
Choose the explanation about the halves matching when folded.
